text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition considers raising taxes after concerns over the 1997 budget. Petroleum tax could be raised by 10 pfennigs.
- Five arrested in connection with kidnapped Frankfurt businessman Jakub Fiszmann.
- Rita Suessmuth, speaker of the lower house of parliament, demands a spiritual and moral revolution.
- The economy has overcome its weaknesses. Dresdner Bank expects 2.5 percent growth.
- Eastern Europe is increasingly important for export
HANDELSBLATT
- German government considers increasing petroleum tax
- Munich Re discloses its financial holdings
- Former boss of troubled shipyard Bremer Vulkan was obliged to act in the interests of the company
- World concept for small trucks under scrutiny. Mercedes Benz make a further step towards globalisation
- Opposition Social Democrats would reverse cuts in sick pay
- Survey of 500 businessmen say Frankfurt could take over from London as Europe's top financial centre
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Bonn puts the brakes on Bavaria's controversial plans to build a dam and canal off the Danube river
- Animal experiments for cosmetics should be banned. Cabinet approves draft for a new law
- Interior Minister Manfred Kather must hand in proposals for making saving by easter
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl discusses BSE crisis with President of the Farmers' Federation Constantin Heereman
DIE WELT
- Bonn plans levying more petroleum tax. Chancellor Helmut Kohl is expected to decide this week
- German investment still increasing abroad
- Mannesmann AG drops its prices of mobile phone costs, last week competitor D1 network cut prices
- Opposition Social Democrats under pressure in row over tax.
- Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt proposes new initiative for telework
